newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Copper tries to erode upside resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Copper tries to erode upside resistance.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
The market is likely to try higher numbers again, but it may need more time to chip away at producer selling which keeps emerging, traders and analysts said.
Aluminium needs to close above $1,600 in order to confirm a break to the upside, they added.
COPPER -
The market had a bit more steam, with fund interest emerging and the cash/threes backwardation widening to over $100.

"The uptrend appears to have rekindled itself in the last few days with a confirmed breach of $2,610 resistance now needed to signal that the next upleg is starting," said broker Brandeis in a commentary.
Only a break below $2,565 support would negate this scenario, it added.
Analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said the fundamentals were bullish, with stocks at 3.8 weeks of consumption and ongoing supply disruptions at Inco, Norilsk and OK Tedi.
Further resistance on the upside was pegged at $2,615 and $2,625.
But a dealer in continental Europe doubted the market was ready to violate the previous $2,609 peak attained on June 12.
"I don't really see it breaking out of this range for the time being. Every time we break lower there's good buying and when it hits $2,600, forward producer selling comes in," he added.
At 0840 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,587/91, barely changed from Wednesday's late close of $2,589/92.
ALUMINIUM -
The market was searching for direction and would have to breach the 10-day moving average at $1,600 to provide upwards momentum.
"I see it as trending sideways with the possibility of a break higher. It might have bottomed out for the time being," a trader said.
Above $1,600, further resistance was pegged at $1,610 and $1,620.
Chartists were still watching to see if a triple top formation would being confirmed, with peaks at $1,651 in late January, $1,701 in early March and $1,679 in mid-May.
But the trader who saw a sideways pattern said a triple bottom could be forming if prices slipped again, with $1,534 in mid February and $1,542 in mid-April.
At 0840 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,590/93, down $4/$3 from Wednesday's late close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
